claims.title: Arithmetic data of the curve
claims.statement: E: y^2 = x^3 - 22735x^2 + 106272484x. Global minimal model y^2 = x^3 - x^2 - 66020924x - 65074271436 via x = X + 7578 (u = 1, same invariant differential). N = 2^3*3*2243*4547^2*5843 = 6503188012738584. Minimal discriminant Delta = 2^8*3^2*2243*4547^3*5843^2 = 16586638656786071143743744 > 0 (two real components); c4 = 3169004368. Kodaira types and Tamagawa numbers: 2: I1* (2); 3: I2 (2), nonsplit, a3 = -1; 2243: I1 (1), split, a2243 = +1; 4547: III (2), a4547 = 0, potentially good supersingular (j = 1728 mod 4547, 4547 = 3 mod 4), inertia of order 4; 5843: I2 (2), nonsplit, a5843 = -1. Tamagawa product 16. E(Q)_tors = Z/2 generated by T = (0,0). Root number w = +1. Good supersingular primes below 2000: 23, 29, 131, 167, 281, 563, 661, 823, 839, 863, 887, 1013, 1471, 1511, 1823. No good prime p is anomalous: #E(F_p) is even and p | #E(F_p) forces p <= 5, while #E(F_5) = 8.

claims.statement: The optimal curve in the isogeny class has Manin constant c0 = 2^a with a <= 8, and 4547 does not divide c0. The seed parametrization has c_E | 2^9. claims.title: What FIN would give: the square-order constraint and the 2601 threshold
claims.statement: If Sha(E/Q) is finite, then #Sha = 9t^2 with t >= 1 and gcd(t, 30030) = 1. The next possible order after 9 is 2601 = 9*17^2, and this is sharp under these inputs: (Z/3)^2 + (Z/17)^2 has order 2601 and carries an alternating perfect pairing.
qualifications: Never hard-code the threshold: it moved 441, 1089, 1521, 2601 as primary components were settled.
claims.label: prop:square

claims.title: A uniform torsion bound is equivalent to the Sha half of the endpoint
claims.statement: Sha(E/Q) is finite of order 9 if and only if #Sha(E/Q)[n] < 2601 for every n >= 1. (Forward: trivial. Converse: the increasing chain Sha[m!] has bounded cardinalities, so it stabilizes and Sha is finite; then S.FIN gives order 9.)
qualifications: An endgame reformulation, not a difficulty reduction.
A uniform bound on Sha[p] over primes alone is insufficient: (Z/3)^2 + (Q_17/Z_17)^2 is a counterexample shape.
claims.label: prop:uniform

claims.title: FIN decomposes by primes, at full depth
claims.statement: FIN holds if and only if every primary component is finite and Sha[p] = 0 for all but finitely many p. Vanishing of Sha[p] implies vanishing of Sha[p^infinity]; finite prime support alone does not control depths or divisible parts.
claims.label: prop:primes

claims.title: Bounded rationality forces q = 36
claims.statement: If q is rational with reduced denominator at most 174, then q = 36. The bound is sharp for this interval: 36 + 1/175 lies in (35.99427, 36.00573).
qualifications: Rationality of q is not known; bounded rationality is equivalent to q = 36 within the interval.
claims.label: prop:ratl

claims.title: Bounded algebraicity forces q = 36
claims.statement: If the primitive irreducible integer polynomial of q has leading coefficient a and other roots q_j with epsilon*|a|*prod|36 - q_j| < 1 (epsilon = 573/100000), then q = 36. Special case: a totally positive algebraic integer of degree at most two, with trace at most 246 in the quadratic case. Trace 247 fails (smaller root of X^2 - 247X + 7595).
claims.label: prop:alg

claims.title: A common scalar would settle both endpoints
claims.statement: Suppose an independently constructed rational B > 0 satisfies q = 4B and, for every prime p, Sha[p^infinity] is finite with v_p(#Sha[p^infinity]) <= v_p(B). Then B = 9 and #Sha = 9, so full BSD(E) holds.
qualifications: Defining B = q/4 assumes the missing arithmeticity; defining B = #Sha assumes FIN and the comparison. Bare existence is an endpoint reformulation.
claims.label: prop:commonB

claims.title: The weighted Mellin period
claims.statement: With alpha_f = 2*pi*i*f(z)dz, l(z) = log(-i*sqrt(N)*z) and gamma the ray from i*infinity to i/sqrt(N): the integral of alpha_f*l^2 over gamma equals L''(E,1)/2 (identity M1). It exists before FIN.

claims.statement: Let p >= 5 be a prime of good ordinary reduction. If C_p := [T^2]L_p(E,T) is a p-adic unit, then Sha(E/Q)[p^infinity] = 0. claims.statement: If Sha(E/Q) is finite, its order is 9.
qualifications: FIN alone permits 9t^2 with gcd(t, 30030) = 1; a proof that #Sha < 2601 given FIN, or the uniform bound (U), would suffice.
Any nonzero bad-prime component would contribute at least 2243^2 to the order.
The uniform bound #Sha[n]<2601 for every n is equivalent to FIN together with ORDER9, not to the conditional assertion ORDER9 alone.
claims.label: open:order9

claims.title: Q36
claims.statement: q = L''(E,1)/(2*Omega_E*Reg) = 36.
qualifications: No p-adic-to-real comparison is currently available; this is narrower than "p-adic work cannot supply FORMULA".
Even q = 36 leaves ORDER9 to prove.
claims.label: open:q36

claims.title: The prime-uniform integral witness (frontier question)
claims.statement: Is some currently p-adic sufficient witness (c_2(p), M_2(p), I_3(p), C_p, ...) the specialization of a single integral, prime-independent object whose nonvanishing or defect is controlled by one fixed integer? A positive answer with the supersingular and bad-prime regimes covered would give finite prime support.
qualifications: In analytic rank one the answer is the Heegner index (conductor-one object); for this curve the corresponding rank-one quantity over Q(sqrt(-23)) is infinite because rank E(K) = 3.
claims.post_master: New formulation since the master record.
claims.label: open:uniform

claims.title: Run013: a qualified full-BSD twist family of 62a1
claims.statement: Conventional 2-isogeny descent for twists of 62a1 by primes q = 5 mod 8 with (q/31) = -1 gives algebraic rank zero and trivial 2-primary Sha (relative natural density 1/8); a qualified full-BSD assembly uses Zhai and Banwait-Huang.
qualifications: Rank-zero chains consume L(E,1) != 0 and do not transfer to this rank-two seed.
claims.label: hist:run013

claims.title: Gate-R: Lean point-group bridge for E_{r,q}
claims.statement: For E_{r,q}: y^2 = x^3 + (1-2r)qx^2 + r^2q^2x, r = +-2^m, m >= 3, under the frozen Params/H41 hypotheses, the Lean chain P01/P03/P04 reaches E_{r,q}(Q)/2E_{r,q}(Q) = Z/2, Gate-R proves rank zero, and the finiteness freeze proves E_{r,q}(Q) finite (finiteness of the rational-point group, not of Sha).
qualifications: Recorded Lean builds; no fresh rebuild in this release (build artifacts were reclaimed).

claims.statement: The lower order calL_p in I^2 is unconditional, but exact order holds only given the c_2 unit. A_2 = 0 is sufficient, not equivalent, for v_p(R_der) >= 0. rho_p = 4 alone does not make c_2(p) a unit: the leading coefficient is #(Sha/Div Sha)(E/K)[p^infinity]*R_der.
